specification.objective: Fix the Firefox-only visual/input coordinate divergence without changing the Kanban implementation by constraining Flutter CanvasKit to one surface on Firefox through the documented web-loader configuration. Preserve default renderer behavior on other browsers and preserve all application/domain contracts.

requirements.statement: Firefox web startup must configure CanvasKit with canvasKitMaximumSurfaces=1 so the app does not depend on Firefox multi-surface canvas composition for ordinary Flutter UI.
Non-Firefox browsers must receive no renderer override from this compatibility policy and continue using Flutter defaults.
The previous canvasKitForceCpuOnly experiment must not return; CPU/GPU selection is independent from the multi-surface composition mechanism implicated by the current evidence.
No Kanban widget, controller, backend, API, domain model, authorization rule, drag/drop behavior, or project workspace component may be changed by this increment.
The custom bootstrap must follow Flutter loader requirements: include {{flutter_js}}, include {{flutter_build_config}}, and call _flutter.loader.load exactly once.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An executable bootstrap harness observes canvasKitMaximumSurfaces=1 for a Firefox user agent and an empty config for a Chromium user agent.
The harness proves canvasKitForceCpuOnly is absent and the loader is invoked exactly once.
The repository diff for this increment is restricted to the bootstrap, its policy test, and this change contract; no Kanban Dart implementation file changes.
The user runtime scenario on Firefox must be re-tested after application because this environment cannot run Flutter or Firefox; POLIS success alone does not claim the visual defect is resolved.

invariants.statement: The exact baseline is remote feature/tasks-kanban commit a039e83b744cadece19da52e14651f9076da0539 with tree ac68a60d7be3853c48e72df484d8f1ba149839ea.
The redesigned Kanban at baseline a039e83 remains untouched; this increment changes only browser initialization policy.
The project metadata identifies Flutter stable revision db50e20168db8fee486b9abf32fc912de3bc5b6a; no SDK or dependency version is changed in this increment.
Chrome/Chromium and other non-Firefox browsers keep the generated Flutter renderer defaults.

forbidden_states.statement: A browser-specific layout offset, transform, padding, hit-test compensation, CSS coordinate patch, or Kanban widget workaround is introduced.
The compatibility setting applies globally to non-Firefox browsers.
Kanban Dart source is modified as part of this renderer-boundary increment.

inputs.statement: After a complete Kanban renderer rewrite at a039e83, Firefox still paints the project toolbar/board at visual coordinates inconsistent with the standard Scaffold/AppBar layout and the user reports that visible controls cannot be clicked.
Earlier forcing CanvasKit CPU-only on Firefox did not resolve the defect, so GPU acceleration is not sufficient as the causal mechanism.
Flutter 3.41.6 uses CanvasKit MultiSurfaceRasterizer by default on Firefox; the project metadata records the 3.41.6 stable revision.
Flutter exposes canvasKitMaximumSurfaces as an official runtime loader configuration for limiting CanvasKit overlay canvases.

outputs.statement: A standards-compliant custom flutter_bootstrap.js that selects a single CanvasKit surface only for Firefox.
Regression coverage that distinguishes the Firefox configuration from the unchanged Chromium/default path.

failure_semantics.statement: If the Firefox single-surface configuration is absent, leaks to Chromium, reintroduces CPU-only rendering, or invokes the loader incorrectly, the regression exits nonzero and emits kanban_firefox_single_surface_missing.
Flutter/Dart and a Firefox runtime are unavailable in this execution environment; runtime visual/input verification remains explicitly pending after artifact validation.
